classification.difficultyReason: Students coordinate the positive-input condition with the transformed logarithmic graph. The hardest part combines an affine input and an affine output with two reflections, requiring students to determine the correct side of the shifted asymptote, the direction of the branch and its placement.

answer.short: Increasing through $(1,0)$ to the right of the asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked: Double the heights on $y=\ln x$. The point $(1,0)$ stays fixed and $(e,1)$ moves to $(e,2)$. Draw the increasing branch on $x>0$.

answer.short: Decreasing through $(-1,0)$ to the left of the asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked: Reflect $y=\ln x$ across the $y$-axis and double the heights. The point $(1,0)$ moves to $(-1,0)$ and $(e,1)$ moves to $(-e,2)$. Draw the decreasing branch on $x<0$.

answer.short: Increasing through $(1,0)$ to the right of the asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked: Halve the heights on $y=\ln x$. The point $(1,0)$ stays fixed and $(e,1)$ moves to $(e,\tfrac12)$. Draw the increasing branch on $x>0$.

answer.short: Decreasing through $(\tfrac12,0)$ to the right of the asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked: Halve the horizontal distances on $y=\ln x$ and reflect across the $x$-axis. The point $(1,0)$ moves to $(\tfrac12,0)$. The branch lies on $x>0$ and rises as $x$ approaches $0$ from the right.

answer.short: Increasing to the right of $x=\tfrac52$, through $(3,3)$, with horizontal intercept at $\tfrac{5+e^{-3/2}}2$.
answer.worked: Write the input as $2(x-\tfrac52)$. Halve the horizontal distances on $y=\ln x$, shift right $\tfrac52$, double the heights, then shift up $3$. The asymptote becomes $x=\tfrac52$ and $(1,0)$ maps to $(3,3)$. For the intercept, set $y=0$, giving $\ln(2x-5)=-\tfrac32$, so $x=\tfrac{5+e^{-3/2}}2$.

answer.short: Increasing to the left of $x=\tfrac52$, through $(2,3)$, with horizontal intercept at $\tfrac{5-e^{3/2}}2$.
answer.worked: Write the input as $-2(x-\tfrac52)$. Halve the horizontal distances on $y=\ln x$, reflect across the $y$-axis, then shift right $\tfrac52$. Double the heights, reflect across the $x$-axis, then shift up $3$. The asymptote becomes $x=\tfrac52$ and $(1,0)$ maps to $(2,3)$. At $x=0$, $y=3-2\ln 5$. Setting $y=0$ gives $\ln(5-2x)=\tfrac32$, so $x=\tfrac{5-e^{3/2}}2$.
